subject: Anatomy
question_text: A middle-aged man presents with right scrotal swelling and pain. On examination, transillumination is positive, and cough impulse is absent. His condition is due to the accumulation of fluid in which layer of the testis?

explanation.text: The clinical scenario is a hydrocele. It is due to accumulation of fluid in the tunica vaginalis of the testis, which is derived from the peritoneum. When the part of the processus vaginalis between the internal inguinal ring and testis fails to obliterate, it forms a communication between the abdominal cavity and scrotum; this may produce congenital inguinal hernia and congenital hydrocele. The source table describes tunica vaginalis, tunica albuginea, and tunica vasculosa.

question_text: A 34-year-old man underwent surgery for an indirect inguinal hernia. During the procedure, the surgeon accidentally injured a nerve which has led to decreased sensation over the anterior one-third region of the scrotum and anteromedial region of the thigh. Which of the following nerves is most likely to be injured?

explanation.text: The genitofemoral nerve is likely to be injured. The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve innervates the anterior one-third of the scrotum, and the femoral branch innervates the anteromedial region of the thigh. Clinical note: considering the root values of nerves supplying the scrotum, the spinal block should be given above L1 to anaesthetise it. The source table summarizes scrotal sensory innervation.

question_text: Which part of the epididymis contains sperms with low amplitude and high-frequency tail movements?

explanation.text: The tail of the epididymis (marked C) contains sperms with low-amplitude and high-frequency tail movements. Sperm motility is important for fertilization, and sperm acquire motility and maturation in the epididymis. The source contrasts high-amplitude/low-frequency and low-amplitude/high-frequency movements and describes the head, body, and tail of the epididymis. Clinical note: cystic degeneration of the epididymis can result in epididymal cysts.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following zones of the prostate primarily encircles the ejaculatory duct?

explanation.text: The central zone of the prostate primarily surrounds the ejaculatory ducts. The source describes three distinct glandular zones: transitional, central, and peripheral. The transitional zone is the most common site for benign prostatic hyperplasia; the central zone surrounds the ejaculatory ducts and is rarely diseased; the peripheral zone is the most common site for prostatic carcinoma. The source notes that some regard fibromuscular stroma as a zone, but Gray's Anatomy 41e describes three distinct glandular zones.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following statements is false about the prostate?

explanation.text: Statements 1, 2 and 5 are false. The prostatic ducts open into the prostatic sinus in the prostatic urethra. The urethral crest is a midline ridge in the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra, with shallow depressions called prostatic sinuses on either side. The glandular prostate contains numerous follicles separated by fibromuscular stroma. These follicles are lined by single-layered or pseudostratified columnar epithelium. Small eosinophilic colloid amyloid bodies called corpora amylacea are frequently seen within follicles. The ducts of prostatic follicles have a basal cuboidal and apical columnar epithelial arrangement. Prostatic secretions are acidic and include acid phosphatase, amylase, prostate-specific antigen (PSA), fibrinolysin, and zinc. Source limitation: the rendered question page shows only combination options referring to statements 1-5; the underlying statements 1-5 are not visibly present and were not reconstructed.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following statements is false about seminal vesicles?

options.label: a
options.text: It is lined by pseudo-stratified columnar epithelium

options.label: b
options.text: It is supplied by inferior vesical artery

options.label: c
options.text: It acts as a storehouse for sperms

correct_answer_text: It acts as a storehouse for sperms

explanation.text:
Seminal vesicles do not store sperms. Seminal vesicles are paired accessory glandular structures of the male reproductive system located at the base of the prostate. The duct of the seminal vesicle joins with vas deferens to form the ejaculatory duct. The mucosa of the seminal vesicle is highly folded and is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium. They secrete white-yellow viscous fluid and contribute to at least two-thirds of the volume of the semen. Secretions are rich in fructose, coagulation proteins, and prostaglandins. They are alkaline

and play an important role in the motility and metabolism of the sperms. The vesiculo-deferential artery, a branch of the umbilical artery is the primary arterial supply of the seminal vesicles. Additional blood supply is from the inferior vesical artery. Venous drainage is by the vesiculo-deferential veins and inferior vesical plexus. Lymphatic drainage is to the internal iliac nodes

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following arteries gives rise to helicine arteries of the penis?

explanation.text: The deep artery of the penis (cavernosal artery) gives rise to the helicine arteries of the penis. They open into the sinusoidal spaces of the corpora cavernosa. The external pudendal artery supplies the skin of the penis. The internal pudendal artery gives perineal and common penile branches; the common penile artery gives bulbourethral, deep penile, and dorsal penile arteries. The source table specifies their territories.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: A patient presented with an enlarged inguinal lymph node. The most likely primary cause is

explanation.text:
The most likely primary cause of an enlarged inguinal lymph node is anal cancer. Lymphatics from the anal canal distal to the dentate line (anal margin) drains into the inguinal lymph nodes. Hence, anal cancer arising distal to dentate line can cause enlarged inguinal lymph nodes. Lymphatics proximal to the dentate line (anal canal) drains into internal iliac lymph nodes through superior rectal lymphatics. Option A: In testicular cancer, lymphatic spread occurs to the paraaortic lymph nodes. Option C: In sigmoid colon cancer, lymphatic spread occurs to the regional lymph node and then to the central lymph node. Option D: In prostate cancer, lymphatic spread occurs to the:

+ Lymph nodes beside the internal iliac vein and in the hollow of the sacrum

+ External iliac lymph nodes.

question_text: A 24-year-old primipara was brought to the ER with lower abdominal pain 6 hours after delivering her baby. On examination pallor and cold clammy skin were present. Pulse was feeble and BP was 70/50 mm Hg. A bedside ultrasound revealed a broad ligament hematoma. Which of the following is not a content of the involved structure?

explanation.text:
The ovaries are not the contents of the broad ligament.

Ovaries are suspended in the pelvic cavity by the mesovarium. It attaches only the hilum of the

ovary to the posterior surface of the broad ligament. The majority of the ovarian surface is covered

by a single layer of cuboidal epithelium which imparts a dull white color to the ovaries.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: The lining epithelium of the fallopian tube is similar to which of the following?

explanation.text:
The lining epithelium of the fallopian tube is a single layer of ciliated columnar epithelium. It is similar to the epithelium of the bronchioles.

The ciliated epithelial cells are predominant in the distal part of the fallopian tube. There is an increase in the height and number of cilia during the estrogenic phase of the menstrual cycle.

Other cells include secretory or peg cells, maximally located in the proximal portion of the tube; these are active around ovulation and their secretions help in capacitation of sperms. Intraepithelial lymphocytes may occasionally be present.

Option A: stomach epithelium is simple columnar. Option B: tracheal epithelium is pseudostratified ciliated columnar. Option D: proximal convoluted tubule epithelium is cuboidal with microvilli.

question_text: Which of the following structures is not related to the posterior surface of the vagina?

explanation.text: Waldeyer's fascia (presacral fascia) forms a posterior relationship of the rectum and is not related to the vagina. It lines the anterior surface of the sacrum. The source table and diagrams describe anterior, posterior, and lateral relations of the vagina.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following gives rise to azygous arteries of the vagina?

explanation.text: The internal iliac artery gives rise to the azygous arteries of the vagina. These are longitudinal median vessels on the anterior and posterior surfaces of the vagina. The vagina also receives blood supply from uterine, internal pudendal, and middle rectal branches of the internal iliac artery.
